AUTHOR: Madokoro, H; Suzuki, M; Tsuji, M; Nagayoshi, T; Nix, S
TITLE: Detection and Recognition of Rare Freshwater Fish with Foundation Models
VENUE: 2025 25TH INTERNATIONAL CONFERENCE ON CONTROL, AUTOMATION AND SYSTEMS, ICCAS
SPECIES: Ginbuna, Tamoroko, Tanago, Aburahaya (0 instances), other fish
DATA: Own FIFISH V6 ROV underwater video, 1,098 still images
V_EV: Sec 2.2: 'The footage was recorded at a depth of 1 m using the FIFISH V6 ROV developed by QYSEA Technology.'
D2: 6:1:3 (train/val/test) of still images extracted from video
D_EV: Sec 2.2: 'the dataset was split into training, validation, and test subsets using a ratio of 6:1:3, respectively.' (images from video, no grouping stated)
R_EV: Sec 3: Grounded SAM 2 applied zero-shot 'without relying on annotations or fine-tuning'; results only qualitative (Figs 9-11)
C_EV: Sec 3.1: 'segmentation experiments conducted with different temperature parameters (0.20, 0.15, 0.10)'; 0.15 chosen by false-positive/missed-detection trade-off
E_EV: Sec 2.4: 'The mean Average Precision (mAP) under an Intersection over Union (IoU) threshold of 0.5 reached 0.91'
ARCH: YOLO-World (S/M/L); Grounded SAM 2 (Grounding DINO Swin-B + SAM 2.1 large)
NOTE: Irrigation pond ROV footage treated as semi-natural freshwater field data; Sec 3 says images from 'a fishery pond' - verifier should confirm it is not aquaculture. Headline YOLO-World results from random image split. R1=Y only via off-the-shelf zero-shot Grounded SAM 2 with qualitative results. 'Temperature' parameter treated as a score threshold with sensitivity analysis (C1=Y, justified -> P); if not regarded as a threshold, C_ALL=NR.
